title: SB150 (132st Legislature (2017-2018)): Prohibit person liable to domestic violence from having firearm

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Ohio) (gun-policy Stage 5, Ohio); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Ohio text (As Introduced (00_IN), ; official copy, https://search-prod.lis.state.oh.us/api/v2/general_assembly_132/legislation/sb150/00_IN/pdf/ (Open States text id 90120339))
provenance.note: As introduced (00_IN); no vote on file. The 'Domestic Violence Survivors Protection Act'. Other marked edits (2903.13, 2919.25, 2919.26, 2923.14, 3113.31) add firearm-prohibition notices and conviction-triggered court steps tied to the same gun ban.

operative_text:
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.13): (6) The person has been convicted of either domestic violence or assault when the victim is a family or household member, whether the offense is classified as a felony or misdemeanor.
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.13): (7) The person is subject to a court order, granted after a full hearing for which the person received notice and an opportunity to be heard, that restrains the person from harassing, stalking, threatening, or engaging in other conduct that would place a family or household member in reasonable fear of bodily injury, or is subject to a temporary protection order issued under section 2919.26 of the Revised Code.
Section 1 (new R.C. 2923.133): (1) Within twenty-four hours after being served with the court order, the offender shall transfer all firearms in the offender's possession or control to a law enforcement agency or federally licensed firearms dealer.
Section 1 (new R.C. 2923.133): (C) An offender who recklessly violates the requirements of this section is guilty of a felony of the fifth degree.
Section 1 (new R.C. 2923.134): (1) Within twenty-four hours after being served with the court order, the respondent shall transfer all firearms in the respondent's possession to a law enforcement agency or federally licensed firearms dealer.
